text: Talat Ahmad, born on 23 December 1955, is an Indian Earth Scientist and former Professor at the Department of Geology, University of Delhi, who also served as Indian National Science Academy (INSA) Senior Scientist. He served as Chairman of the Governing Body overseeing the Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology, Dehradun from 1 December 2021 (full charge from 1 June 2022) until 30 November 2024, and thereafter continued as a member of the Governing Body (WIHG) from 1 December 2024 to 30 November 2027. He previously served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Kashmir from 6 August 2018 to 20 May 2022, marking his second tenure, and had earlier held the position from 1 June 2011 to 2014, taking over from Professor Riyaz Punjabi. Before that, he served as Vice-Chancellor of Jamia Millia Islamia, though he resigned a few months short of his full term, following a search committee headed by Prof. Abid Hussain, former Indian ambassador to the US, and including Prof. G. K. Chadha, Prof. Seyed E. Hasnain, and other eminent figures. He is the first Vice-Chancellor to serve a second term and the second to be appointed from outside Jammu and Kashmir in the past two decades, with Jalees Ahmad Khan Tareen being the first such appointee from outside the state (2001–2004). Ahmad was born and raised in Giridih, Jharkhand, and his father was Moinuddin Ahmad. He completed his schooling at Giridih Higher Secondary School, joined Aligarh Muslim University in 1972 for a BSc in geology (completed 1975), pursued an MSc in geology (1977), M.Phil in Ore Petrology from Jawaharlal Nehru University (1980), and a PhD in Igneous Petrology from JNU (1985). He held postdoctoral fellowships at the University of Leicester (1988–89) under a Government of India Fellowship, the University of Cambridge (1997–98) under the Natural Environment Research Council (NERC), and Nagoya University, Japan (1999–2000) under the Japanese Society for Promotion of Science (JSPS). In 1979, he was selected by the UPSC and joined the Geological Survey of India (GSI) in February 1980, working there for a year before leaving due to its survey-oriented nature. He then worked as a Scientist at the Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology, Dehradun from 16 July 1984 to 3 September 1989, and served as a scientist under DST for nineteen years (1984–2003). He joined the Department of Geology, University of Delhi as a professor on 31 October 2003, where he initiated research projects in central India and Rajasthan, and later secured a project from the Russian Foundation for Basic Research (RFBR) in the Kashmir valley. He was appointed Vice-Chancellor of Jamia Millia Islamia on 29 April 2014, taking over from Prof. S M Sajid and succeeding Najeeb Jung, who became the 20th Lieutenant Governor of Delhi in April 2013, and was relieved by A M Shah, dean of academic affairs. Ahmad has over 65 research publications and has supervised numerous M.Phil. and PhD research studies at the University of Delhi and the Research School of Earth Sciences, Australian National University, Canberra. He has led several sponsored projects, including Geochemical, Isotopic and Geochronological characterisation of Granotoids from the Central Indian Tectonic Zones (CITZ) and Central Indian Shear Zones (CISZ)—Constraints on Pre-Cambrian Crystal Evolution, funded by Indo-Russian collaboration and the ILTP Project, and Proterozoic mafic magmatism in the Central Indian Tectonic Zone (CITZ): elemental and isotopic constraints on crystal evolution and geodynamics. He is a member of several prestigious societies and has received numerous fellowships and awards.
